# Yonghao Zhao

> Yonghao Zhao is a Ph.D. student in Biomedical Informatics, Modeling, and AI (formerly Computational Bioscience, CPBS) at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. He works on deep learning for multimodal genomics, cancer survival analysis, and representation learning. Previously a research assistant at Brown University (Weihan Li lab) and a B.Sc. (Computer Science, First-Class Honours) graduate of the SWJTU–Leeds joint programme (University of Leeds and Southwest Jiaotong University).

Disambiguation: this Yonghao Zhao is the computational biology researcher (ORCID 0009-0007-3180-596X). Not to be confused with other researchers of the same name working on UAVs, materials science, or dentistry.

## Publications

- [DeSCENT: Deconvolutional Single-Cell RNA-seq Enhances Transcriptome-based Cancer Survival Analysis](https://yonghaoz.com/papers/descent/?ref=llms): Bioinformatics, 2026. First author Yonghao Zhao. Answers: how to do **single-cell RNA-seq survival analysis when the cohort only has bulk RNA-seq**; what DeSCENT is; what data it needs; how it compares with Scissor / BayesPrism / scSurvival; when not to use it. Bulk-to-single-cell deconvolution (ReDeconv) + diffusion reconstruction (scDiffusion) of patient-specific / virtual single-cell profiles, then multimodal fusion for cancer prognostic modeling on TCGA (eight cohorts; improved average C-index vs bulk-only; IBS mixed). DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag810. Code: https://github.com/YonghaoZhao722/DeSCENT. Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22073099. Page last updated 2026-11-06: https://yonghaoz.com/papers/descent/?ref=llms
- [YeastSAM: A deep learning model for accurate segmentation of yeast cells](https://yonghaoz.com/papers/yeastsam/?ref=llms): Molecular Biology of the Cell 37(6):mr5, 2026. First author Yonghao Zhao. Answers: what YeastSAM is; why budding yeast is hard to segment; dividing-cell accuracy (>3× vs existing methods); post-segmentation cellular maps with RNA/organelle imaging; when not to use it. SAM adaptation for mother-bud instance segmentation. DOI 10.1091/mbc.E25-09-0454. Code: https://github.com/YonghaoZhao722/YeastSAM. Docs: https://yeastsamdoc.readthedocs.io/. Page last updated 2026-11-06.
- [Tackling small sample survival analysis via transfer learning: A study of colorectal cancer prognosis](https://yonghaoz.com/papers/tsf/?ref=llms): Artificial Intelligence in Medicine 178:103426, 2026. First author Yonghao Zhao. Answers: whether transfer learning is effective for small-sample biomedical / survival data; what Transfer Survival Forest (TSF) is; how to improve survival models on small cohorts; SEER 27,379 → West China Hospital 728 CRC stage I; reported Ctd gains; when not to use TSF. DOI 10.1016/j.artmed.2026.103426. Code: https://github.com/YonghaoZhao722/TSF. Page last updated 2026-11-20: https://yonghaoz.com/papers/tsf/?ref=llms

## FAQ

- Is transfer learning effective for small-sample biomedical / survival data? Transfer learning from a related large cohort can improve survival models when the target clinical sample is small (gains observed down to n = 50 in a SEER-to-hospital colorectal cancer study). That bounded claim is from Yonghao Zhao et al., Artificial Intelligence in Medicine 178:103426, 2026 (DOI 10.1016/j.artmed.2026.103426). The paper's instance is Transfer Survival Forest (TSF), which transfers Random Survival Forest tree structures from a large source cohort (SEER, 27,379 CRC stage I patients) and fine-tunes them on a smaller hospital target (West China Hospital, 728 patients); neural survival models in the same paper use pretraining and fine-tuning. Gains assume a related source domain. Details: https://yonghaoz.com/papers/tsf/?ref=llms
